tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. content.content:
### The numbers this plan is priced against

- **Decode: 34.2 tok/s through the server** (~29 ms a step), and the step is
  *latency, not bandwidth*: single-wave workgroups that all fit at once (P8).
  That is why rows are cheap. **A two-row pass costs 1.32 steps at 48 layers**
  (P5c), and the MoE is the part that keeps growing (10 experts touched at
  M = 1, 17 at 2, 36 at 4).
- **Prefill: ~1200 tok/s**, and a unit of work is a whole `-llm-batch` chunk.
  At the served 8192 that is **~6-7 s that nothing else can interrupt**.
- **Memory:** the served 262k configuration stages at ~83 GB and leaves ~33 GB.
  Two more full-context sequences would need 14.5 GB of KV plus 0.24 GB of
  DeltaNet state. That fits, with ~18 GB to spare.
- **`maxStorageBufferRange` is 4 GiB - 4**, and a K or V plane is 12 KB a cell,
  so **one plane buffer holds ~349k cells in total**. If slots share a buffer
  by offset, `slots × ctx ≤ ~349k` (for example 3 × 112k). Three full 262k
  contexts need a buffer per slot, bound as a descriptor array (C6), like the
  MoE bank's.

## The design, in one paragraph

**Slots, then a scheduler, then batching.** The graph gets `S` *sequence
slots*: `S` copies of the per-sequence state above, one live at a time,
switched by `Graph.UseSlot` (C1). The backend replaces its mutex with a
**scheduler that owns the graph** and interleaves *work units*: a decode step
or a prefill chunk, each on some slot. It picks the next unit by priority
class and then round-robin (C2). This is concurrency without extra
throughput: three streams share ~34 tok/s. What it buys is that nobody waits
for someone else's whole generation, and a voice command waits at most one
work unit. Making that unit short is C3. **Batching (C5)** then runs the
decoding slots' next tokens as **R rows of one pass**. Every block but
attention, DeltaNet and PLE is already row-independent, and P5b built the
R-row decode GEMVs. It is the step that adds throughput: if three rows cost
~1.5 steps, three streams get ~23 tok/s each instead of ~11.
**Checkpoints (C4)** make prefix caching work across more than one live
conversation, and between the turns of a voice session.

## Priority

Two classes, **interactive** and **background**. The API names the class:

- `service_tier` on the request body (OpenAI's field on chat completions and
  responses): `"priority"` is interactive; `"flex"`, `"default"` or absent
  are background, unless the server's default says otherwise.
- An `X-Priority: interactive|background` header, for a client that cannot
  add a body field (Home Assistant's OpenAI integration is the likely one).
- A server flag for the default class.

Scheduling rules (C2, tuned in C3):

1. An interactive unit always runs before a background one. Preemption
   happens at a **unit boundary**, never mid-pass. The activation arenas are
   shared, so a pass cannot be paused.
2. Within a class, round-robin **by GPU time**, not by unit count (deficit
   round-robin). A prefill chunk is worth ~200 decode steps.
3. Background prefill is cut into `-llm-preempt-chunk` pieces whenever there
   is more than one slot. It cannot wait until an interactive request is live,
   because by then the chunk it waits behind has already started. So the worst
   wait an interactive request sees is one short chunk rather than 6-7 s, and
   what that costs background prefill is C3's measurement.
4. Decode steps of one class share a pass (C5, done). Background rows do
   **not** ride in an interactive pass: one rider would cost the voice
   stream 1.47x and two 1.83x, and a voice reply's latency is its TTFT.
5. At most `S` requests hold slots. A fourth waits for one, and it is logged
   as queued, as today.

## Stages

Each stage has a gate that can fail, and the gate lands in the same commit as
the change.

| # | stage | what it is | gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~~**C0**~~ | ~~**Instrument**~~ **done 2026-09-23** (below): `cmd/loadgen` | A load generator (`cmd/bench -llm-concurrent` or similar) that fires one voice-shaped request (a fixed ~2k-token system prompt + a short utterance, short answer) against two agent-shaped ones (long prompts, long answers). It records per-stream TTFT, token rate and total throughput. Run it against today's server for the baseline. | Numbers in this file, two runs agreeing. |
| ~~**C1**~~ | ~~**Sequence slots in the graph**~~ **done 2026-09-23** (below) | `GraphOpts.Slots`, `Graph.UseSlot(s)`. Attention allocates `S×` the cache and offsets it by slot; DeltaNet and PLE allocate `S` state/ring slots, and the *committed slot* is the sequence slot. The graph keeps `past`, `ids` and the recorded decode step per slot. Refused together with `Speculative` (the ping-pong and the slots share an index). | `TestGraphSlotsAreSequences`: two sequences interleaved token by token through one graph give **bit-identical** logits to each run alone, prerecorded decode included. Its control (the same interleave without switching slots) must differ. |
| ~~**C2**~~ | ~~**The scheduler**~~ **done 2026-09-23** (below); `-llm-slots` stays 1 in `ai.service` until C0/C3 are measured | `backend.LLM` gets a scheduler goroutine that owns the graph. `Complete` submits work and receives tokens. Slot choice: longest reusable held prefix, else the least recently used idle slot. `held` becomes per slot. Priority from `service_tier`/header/flag. `-llm-slots N` (default 1 until C3 lands). | An `api`-level test with three concurrent requests on the 4-layer prefix: each one's output equals its solo run at temperature 0. The interactive one's TTFT is bounded by one unit, not by the other requests' generations. |
| ~~**C3**~~ | ~~**Bounded work units**~~ **measured 2026-09-23** (below); chunk stays 2048 until C4 | Price prefill against chunk size at depth (512 / 1024 / 2048 / 4096 / 8192). While an interactive request is live, cap background chunks at the chosen size. Measure the switch cost between slots (per-slot recorded decode steps should make it ~0). | C0's harness: interactive TTFT and token rate with two background streams live, against the same request alone. |
| ~~**C4**~~ | ~~**Checkpoints: prefix caching across threads**~~ **done 2026-09-23** within a slot (below); cross-slot restore not built | Snapshot a slot's carried state at a **stable boundary**: the end of everything before the last user message. That is DeltaNet state + rings (~120 MB, ~1 ms on-device), the PLE ring, the pooled indexer block that straddles the boundary, and the position. KV cells below the boundary are never rewritten by a continuation, so within a slot they need no copy. A request whose prompt shares the checkpointed prefix restores it and prefills only the tail. That fixes the voice case (same system prompt, new utterance) and agents that retry or branch. Cross-slot restore copies the KV cells too (27.8 KB a cell, ~0.11 GB for 4k). | Restore-then-continue is **bit-identical** to a fresh prefill of the whole prompt, and a control that skips the DeltaNet restore differs. |
| ~~**C5**~~ | ~~**Batched decode**~~ **done 2026-09-23** (below): per-row passes rather than row-aware kernels, and `moe.up` skips padding rows | R decoding slots advance one token each in one pass. Per-row position and slot come from an arena table (P1c's trick again: the recorded buffer stays byte-identical). The row-aware kernels are attention (`pack`, `idx`, `score`, `select`, the gathered `wmma`), DeltaNet (`conv`, `scan`, `seq_hist`) and PLE's `hist`. Raise `GEMVMaxRows` 2 → 3 with its rung in `TestGraphIsAChunkSplit` in the same commit (see the memory note on new row counts). **C5a prices it first**: a 3-row pass at 48 layers against a 1-row one, which needs the machine (stop `ai.service`). | Each row of a batched pass equals that slot's solo step (to the R-row GEMV's documented tolerance), whole graph, at R = 2 and 3. |
| ~~**C6**~~ | ~~**Full context in every slot**~~ **done 2026-09-23** (below): a buffer set and a pipeline set a slot, no descriptor array | K, V and indexer planes as a descriptor array of per-slot buffers (`PipelineSpec.Counts`, as the MoE bank does), which lifts the `slots × ctx ≤ ~349k` cap to 3 × 262k (~22 GB of KV). | `TestAttnGPUCacheSizeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` extended across slots; P18's recall at 237k in a non-zero slot. |
| C7 | *Mixed passes* (maybe) | Decode rows riding in another slot's prefill chunk, so a background prefill does not stall the other streams' decode. Only worth building if C3's numbers leave background decode visibly starved. | — |

Not planned: a second Vulkan queue or global-priority queues to preempt a
pass mid-flight. The arenas are shared, so preemption would need a second set
of them, and C3's short chunks bound the same latency far more cheaply.

## Open questions for later stages

- **How long is Home Assistant's system prompt?** C4's value and C3's chunk
  cap both depend on it. One real request in the journal answers it. The
  harness assumes 1.94k tokens (40 devices).
- ~~**The preempt chunk, 2048 or 1024?**~~ **Decided 2026-09-23: 2048.**
  A voice command's worst wait of ~2 s while an agent prefills is fine;
  what is not fine is minutes, so prefill speed wins over a second of
  latency.
- ~~**Default slot count and context per slot.**~~ **Decided 2026-09-23:
  three slots**, and with C6 each holds the full 262 144 cells
  (`ai.service`'s LLM line, `-llm-slots 3`).
- ~~**Does a background stream riding in a voice decode pass (rule 4) cost
  the voice reply too much?**~~ C5's numbers: one rider costs it 1.47x and
  two cost 1.83x. It stays off, because a voice reply is short and its
  latency is its TTFT, which riding does not help.

-----
## C5 — batched decode (done 2026-09-23)

`llm.Graph.DecodeRows(slots, ids)` advances several sequences one token each
in one pass. The scheduler batches the pending decode steps of one class into
it.

**How, and why not row-aware kernels.** The plan was to make attention,
DeltaNet and PLE read a per-row slot and position from an arena table. The
build runs **those three blocks' per-sequence kernels once per row instead**,
as a one-token pass of that row's sequence: its slot's cache, state and
ring, its row of the projection in and its row of the context out. The
projections, the hyper-connections, the MoE and the head run over all R rows
at once. Three things make this nearly free:

- **The position was the only thing a push field had no room for.**
  `SEQ_PAST` is now `actu[pc.lowRank]`: dword 1+r of the block's arena for
  row r, and dword 0 for every ordinary dispatch, whose `lowRank` was
  already zero. None of the thirteen kernels that read the position uses
  `lowRank` as itself. So a single-sequence pass and its recorded replay are
  the same bytes as before. `TestGraphLogits` reproduces P16's diagnostics
  to the digit (maxAbs 1.987e+00 at 19208, rms 3.314e-01).
- **The recorded pass fences every dispatch**, so every scratch arena
  between the projection and the context is reused row after row. A row's
  pass may write the context's pad rows past itself, and the next row's pass
  overwrites them, because rows run in ascending order.
- **Per-row cost is small at decode**: attention and DeltaNet add ~2.4 ms a
  row at 48 layers (the batch profile below). Row-aware kernels would win
  back part of that, and it is the smaller lever.

**`moe.up` computed padding rows.** The GEMV rung computes `ROWS` rows of
every expert tile, and the permutation's sentinel makes the extra ones
harmless. At P5b's two rows of one sequence that was nearly free, because
most tiles had two real rows. With three conversations most of the ~27
experts serve one row, so two-thirds of `moe.up`'s arithmetic was padding.
The tile record's third word (the block size, which nothing read) is now the
real row count (`llm_moe_perm.comp`, and on the host for the shared expert's
list), and `llm_moe_gemv.comp` stops at it. `moe.up` at three rows went from
**28.9 to 18.8 ms**, and a three-row pass from **64.2 to 53.4 ms**. The
shared expert reads ~0.25 ms slower at three rows in both runs, which is not
explained.

**The instrument is `cmd/llm -batch 1,2,3 -batch-depth 7000`.** It uses one
slot a row, each prefilled with its own wikitext, and decodes greedily. A
fixed token per row would read the same experts every step and understate
the MoE; that was C5a's error in another form. `-batch-chunk 8192 -batch-ctx
65536` gives the server's shape, which costs the same to 0.6 ms.

| rows | pass | a row | aggregate | moe | dn | attn | distinct experts (layer 47) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 29.2 ms | 34.2 tok/s | 34.2 | 11.1 | 6.8 | 3.4 | 10.0 |
| 2 | 42.9 (1.47x) | 23.3 | 46.6 | 20.5 | 7.8 | 4.8 | 19.2 |
| 3 | **53.4 (1.83x)** | 18.7 | **56.2** | 28.7 | 8.9 | 6.1 | 26.8 |

**Gates:**
- `TestGraphDecodeRowsIsEachSlot` (4 layers, 5 s): three sequences of 700,
  300 and 500 tokens decode 8 steps batched. Every row's logits are
  **bit-identical** to that sequence stepped alone, at three rows and at two
  (slots 0 and 2). There is nothing to reassociate: the R-row GEMV sums each
  row in the one-row order, and the per-sequence kernels run a row as a
  one-token pass. The three controls each make row 1 read row 0's position
  in one block, and each moves the logits: attention 0.169 rms, DeltaNet
  0.127, PLE 0.055.
- `GEMVMaxRows` 3 with its rungs: `TestGraphIsAChunkSplit` gained the
  unpinned "2 / 3 at a time, on the decode schedule" subtests (C5a's).
  `TestDeltaNetGPUStateCarries` now pins the GEMM, because its 3 + 4 split
  made the first half a GEMV. `TestMoEGPUDecode` and `TestMoEGPUSharedPlan`
  now stage one past the bound. They staged a literal two, so their
  "refused past the bound" control was passing on the staging's refusal and
  not the plan's.
- `TestLLMConcurrentIsSolo` (backend) now asserts that batching happened:
  23 batched passes of 2.91 rows each, and every conversation streams
  exactly its solo text.

**At 48 layers** (C0's harness, same hour, two runs agreeing within 0.7
tok/s):

| | agents' decode, each | agents done | aggregate | voice |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 agents, batching off | 11.0-11.5 tok/s | 88.0 s | 26.2 tok/s | — |
| **3 agents, batching on** | **17.6-18.8** | **62.0 s** | **37.1** | — |
| C0's mix, batching off | 16.9 / 16.4 | 61.1 s | 26.2 | as C4 |
| **C0's mix, batching on** | **23.2 / 22.3** | **48.6 s** | **32.9** | as C4 (0.20 s in decode) |

- The loop's gap between batched steps is **0.3 ms** (an env-gated trace in
  a scratch build). The coalescing wait (up to 5 ms for peers that are still
  sampling) costs nothing measurable, and without it the first conversation
  back from sampling would run alone.
- **Background rows still do not ride in an interactive pass** (rule 4).
  Per the table, one rider would cost a voice stream 1.47x and two 1.83x.
  That stays off: a voice reply is 10-30 tokens, and its latency is its TTFT.
- `-llm-batch-decode=false` is the control.
- **Solo decode is 33.8 tok/s this afternoon against 34.7 this morning, and
  the same-hour A/B/C says that is not this work.** The one-row pass is 29.0
  ms before today's changes, 29.3 with `MAXROWS` 3 and 29.5 now, inside the
  0.5 ms spread.

## C6 — full context in every slot (done 2026-09-23)

**Each slot's cache is its own three buffers (key, value, indexer), and each
slot has its own attention pipelines.** A pipeline's descriptor set names its
buffers, so a slot with buffers of its own needs pipelines of its own. The
plan's descriptor array (`PipelineSpec.Counts`, as the MoE bank does) would
have needed the slot index in every cache-reading kernel, and the push block
has no room for it. Instead `AttnGPU.build` runs once per slot against that
slot's buffers, and `UseSlot` swaps the buffers and the pipeline map. The
cache offsets no longer depend on the slot, **no shader changed**, and a
recorded pass was already mixing pipelines of different blocks. So:

- `maxStorageBufferRange` caps a slot's cells (~349k), not all slots'
  together. **3 × 262 144 cells**, where C1's shared buffers allowed
  ~349k in total.
- The pipeline builds cost nothing measurable. The 48-layer server came up
  in 68 s against P18's ~66, because identical SPIR-V hits Mesa's shader
  cache. Residency is **~98 GB, with 19 GB available** on this 117.7 GiB
  machine.
- Batched decode (C5) needed nothing: a row's per-sequence core already
  calls `UseSlot` for its slot.

**Gates:**
- `TestAttnGPUSlotsHaveTheirOwnCache` (block, 0.5 s): slot 2 prefills half
  the 4k fixture, slot 0 runs a different input from cell zero, and slot 2
  continues. The continuation is **bit-identical** to the same two chunks
  with nothing in between. The control puts slot 2's continuation on slot
  0's pipelines, and it moves from the first continued token. A fresh run
  cannot see a shared cache, because it writes every cell it reads; the
  first version of this control put one inside
  `TestAttnGPUCacheSizeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer` and passed unchanged, which
  is how that was found.

### The numbers this plan is priced against

- **Decode: 34.2 tok/s through the server** (~29 ms a step), and the step is
  *latency, not bandwidth*: single-wave workgroups that all fit at once (P8).
  That is why rows are cheap. **A two-row pass costs 1.32 steps at 48 layers**
  (P5c), and the MoE is the part that keeps growing (10 experts touched at
  M = 1, 17 at 2, 36 at 4).
- **Prefill: ~1200 tok/s**, and a unit of work is a whole `-llm-batch` chunk.
  At the served 8192 that is **~6-7 s that nothing else can interrupt**.
- **Memory:** the served 262k configuration stages at ~83 GB and leaves ~33 GB.
  Two more full-context sequences would need 14.5 GB of KV plus 0.24 GB of
  DeltaNet state. That fits, with ~18 GB to spare.
- **`maxStorageBufferRange` is 4 GiB - 4**, and a K or V plane is 12 KB a cell,
  so **one plane buffer holds ~349k cells in total**. If slots share a buffer
  by offset, `slots × ctx ≤ ~349k` (for example 3 × 112k). Three full 262k
  contexts need a buffer per slot, bound as a descriptor array (C6), like the
  MoE bank's.

## The design, in one paragraph

**Slots, then a scheduler, then batching.** The graph gets `S` *sequence
slots*: `S` copies of the per-sequence state above, one live at a time,
switched by `Graph.UseSlot` (C1). The backend replaces its mutex with a
**scheduler that owns the graph** and interleaves *work units*: a decode step
or a prefill chunk, each on some slot. It picks the next unit by priority
class and then round-robin (C2). This is concurrency without extra
throughput: three streams share ~34 tok/s. What it buys is that nobody waits
for someone else's whole generation, and a voice command waits at most one
work unit. Making that unit short is C3. **Batching (C5)** then runs the
decoding slots' next tokens as **R rows of one pass**. Every block but
attention, DeltaNet and PLE is already row-independent, and P5b built the
R-row decode GEMVs. It is the step that adds throughput: if three rows cost
~1.5 steps, three streams get ~23 tok/s each instead of ~11.
**Checkpoints (C4)** make prefix caching work across more than one live
conversation, and between the turns of a voice session.

## Priority

Two classes, **interactive** and **background**. The API names the class:

- `service_tier` on the request body (OpenAI's field on chat completions and
  responses): `"priority"` is interactive; `"flex"`, `"default"` or absent
  are background, unless the server's default says otherwise.
- An `X-Priority: interactive|background` header, for a client that cannot
  add a body field (Home Assistant's OpenAI integration is the likely one).
- A server flag for the default class.

Scheduling rules (C2, tuned in C3):

1. An interactive unit always runs before a background one. Preemption
   happens at a **unit boundary**, never mid-pass. The activation arenas are
   shared, so a pass cannot be paused.
2. Within a class, round-robin **by GPU time**, not by unit count (deficit
   round-robin). A prefill chunk is worth ~200 decode steps.
3. Background prefill is cut into `-llm-preempt-chunk` pieces whenever there
   is more than one slot. It cannot wait until an interactive request is live,
   because by then the chunk it waits behind has already started. So the worst
   wait an interactive request sees is one short chunk rather than 6-7 s, and
   what that costs background prefill is C3's measurement.
4. Decode steps of one class share a pass (C5, done). Background rows do
   **not** ride in an interactive pass: one rider would cost the voice
   stream 1.47x and two 1.83x, and a voice reply's latency is its TTFT.
5. At most `S` requests hold slots. A fourth waits for one, and it is logged
   as queued, as today.

name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata:

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a

four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see

name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.

Set it and staging is a disk read instead:

    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache

With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.

**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
That part is unavoidable today.

**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
of a ~31 ms token.

**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

name: auto-committer-owns-main
description: "An external process auto-commits the strix-halo-vulkan working tree to main every ~30-45 min with the message \"ai\", and other sessions edit the same tree concurrently, so `go build ./...` can fail on someone else's half-written file."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8382387e-ec90-4d7d-8642-1d65b8bbd10a
  modified: 2026-09-17T23:25:30.192Z
---

In `~/repos/strix-halo-vulkan` something outside the session commits the whole
working tree to `main` on a timer — the message is always `ai`, and the commits
land roughly every 30-45 minutes (observed 18:53, 19:37, 21:02, 21:36 on
2026-09-14). So a `git add -A && git commit` at the end of a session will often
print **"nothing to commit, working tree clean"** even though the work is
unsaved-looking: check `git show --stat HEAD` before concluding anything was
lost. There is an `origin` (github.com:theninj4/strix-halo-vulkan) but `main`
has **no upstream**, so nothing is pushed.

**Other sessions edit this tree at the same time.** On 2026-09-18 a second
session was mid-refactor in `zimage/pipeline` and mid-write in `api/images.go`
while this one built `embed/`: `go build ./...` failed twice on *their*
undefined symbols (`p.latentH`, `formatSize`), minutes apart, and both cleared
on their own. Check `git status --short` and file mtimes before believing a
build break is yours, and build the packages you touched
(`go build ./embed/ ./api/ …`) rather than `./...` while it lasts.

**Why:** the commit log is therefore not the project's narrative — `TODO.md`
is, and every session appends a handoff to it. That is why the repo's own docs
say to read `TODO.md`/the current vertical file first.

**How to apply:** don't branch before committing here (the whole history is
direct-to-main), don't amend the `ai` commits to "improve" them, and put the
session's story in `TODO.md` rather than in a commit message. Edit files with
targeted replacements rather than whole-file rewrites when another session may
be in the same file, and never "fix" a symbol that belongs to their in-flight
work. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and [[phase-2-pivot-to-pipeline]] for what
the docs expect a session to record.

name: ai-service-user-unit
description: "The ai server runs as a --user systemd unit on :11434; logs are journalctl --user -u ai, deploy.sh installs it, startup takes ~25 s, and it is deliberately served open with -token=."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

The `serve` binary runs as a **user** systemd unit, not a system one, and not
in the foreground:

- **Install/redeploy: `./deploy.sh`.** It builds `./ai` from `./cmd/serve`,
  substitutes the unit's `###` placeholder with `$(pwd)`, writes
  `~/.config/systemd/user/ai.service`, `daemon-reload`s and restarts.
  `./ai.service` in the repo is a *template*, not a script — running it gives
  `Permission denied`, which is the expected outcome, not a bug to fix.
- **`deploy.sh` ends with `journalctl --user -n 100 -f -u ai`,** which never
  returns. In an agent session run its steps by hand and skip the tail.
- **Logs: `journalctl --user -u ai`** (`--user` is required; it is invisible to
  the system journal). The server logs one line per backend at startup and
  `listening on http://0.0.0.0:11434` when all of them are up.
- **Startup is ~25 s** and ~13 GB peak, nearly all of it the Z-Image backend;
  tts/stt/embed land in the first 3 s. Don't conclude anything from the log
  before the image line.
- **State without tailing:**
  `systemctl --user show ai.service -p ActiveState -p SubState -p NRestarts`.
  The unit ships `Restart=always` + `RestartSec=1`, and the server `log.Fatal`s
  on any bad flag or missing checkpoint, so a config mistake becomes a silent
  ~26 s crash loop. A non-zero `NRestarts` (or "restart counter is at N" in the
  journal) is the tell; `systemctl --user reset-failed ai.service` before a
  fixed redeploy so the count reads clean.
- **Auth: omitting `-token` does not disable it.** The flag *defaults* to a
  non-empty token (`defaultToken` in `cmd/serve/main.go`), so a unit that says
  nothing about tokens requires a bearer header on every `/v1` request. Only an
  explicitly empty `-token=` opens the server. This cost an afternoon once.
- **The deployed unit runs `-token=` on purpose**, chosen 2026-09-18: open, no
  bearer header, on `0.0.0.0:11434` so the second machine can reach it. Don't
  "fix" the empty token back to a default — it is the configuration that was
  asked for. See [[deployment-two-machines]].
- The unit is **`disabled`** as of 2026-09-18 — it does not come back on boot
  or login without `systemctl --user enable ai` and `loginctl enable-linger`.

Anchor journal reads to the *current* instance
(`journalctl --user -u ai --since "@$(date -d "$(systemctl --user show
ai.service -p ExecMainStartTimestamp --value)" +%s)"`). A plain `--since -2min`
still contains the previous instance's crash lines and will make an
until-loop fire on a failure that is already fixed — the same self-matching
trap as [[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]]. See
[[deployment-two-machines]] for which box this is meant to run on and
[[gpu-debugging-access]] for when it hangs rather than exits.

**The LLM line (P18, 2026-09-22)** is `-llm -llm-ctx 262144 -llm-batch 8192`: the full trained context, ~66 s and ~83 GB to come up. See [[llm-full-context-262k]].

name: never-edit-source-during-a-sweep
description: "`go run` rebuilds on every invocation, so editing repo source while a multi-arm benchmark script is running kills every arm after the one already in flight."
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

**2026-09-21.** A four-arm 48-layer depth sweep lost three of its four arms.
The script called `go run ./cmd/llm` once per arm; arm 1 had already built and
ran fine; while it ran I edited `shaders/shaders.go` to add a new `//go:embed`
for a `.spv` that did not exist yet, and arms 2-4 each died instantly with

    shaders/shaders.go:2646:12: pattern llm_attn_expand.spv: no matching files found

~25 minutes of measurement, and the failure was silent in the sweep's own log
until the end.

[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] already says "edit *text* while it runs, nothing
else" — that rule is about CPU contention perturbing the numbers. This is a
second, harder reason: **a multi-arm script that invokes `go run` rebuilds the
tree at the start of every arm**, so the source it compiles is whatever the
tree holds *then*, not what it held at launch. Even an edit that compiles
would silently measure a different binary in later arms, which is worse than
a crash.

**How to apply:** make the benchmark script `go build -o <scratchpad>/bench
./cmd/llm` **once at the top** and run that binary for every arm. Then the
tree is free to edit while it runs, and every arm is provably the same build.
Select arms with environment variables read at dispatch time (this is what
`LLM_ATTN_SPLITS` and `LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS` are for), never by rebuilding.

name: prefill-rates
description: "Prompt-processing rates after P12 (2026-09-21), the ubatch curve and the decode cost that comes with it, what the MoE prefill GEMM is bound by, and the four prefill ideas that are measured dead."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d77f87a5-b722-4ac5-aaa9-d322f713f1da
  modified: 2026-09-21T22:34:23.069Z
---

**Prefill does not plateau where llama.cpp's does, so the ubatch is a real
knob — but widening it is a trade, not a free win.** 48 layers, shipped banks,
two runs each (`results/p12_pp_*.csv`, write-ups `research/p11-prefill.md` and
`research/p12-prefill-round-two.md`):

**Superseded at depth by P14 (2026-09-22)** — see [[long-context-prefill-128k]]
for the rates against context depth, which are no longer these. The depth-zero
ladder below stands.

| ubatch | P11 | P12 | vs llama.cpp |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 681.7 | 683.3 | 1.75x |
| 2048 | 1191.8 | **1207.7** | 3.08x |
| 4096 | 1340.7 | 1363.5 | 3.48x |
| 8192 | 1372.2 | **1403.9** | **3.59x** |

Against **context depth** at ubatch 2048: 1154.6 / 968.1 / 894.3 / 805.7 /
**667.7** tok/s at 0 / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k. Arms are reproducible to
0.1-0.5%, so a 1.2% difference is real; quote means of two passes.

**`-llm-batch` defaults to 4096 and, since P16 (2026-09-22), a wider batch
costs memory and nothing else.** P12-7 measured 4096 costing 8% of decode
through the server and P15 11-22% at depth; **that was a bug** — the DeltaNet
and attention input ports zero-padded a decode step out to the whole arena.
Fixed, through the server (four ~4k prompts, 256 generated, two passes to 0.1%):

| batch | prefill | decode |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 1052.2 | 34.19 |
| 4096 | 1198.5 | 34.20 |
| 8192 | 1232.5 | 34.16 |

8192 only helps prompts > 4096 tokens, holds ~3 GB more, and lowers the
`maxStorageBufferRange` context cap. See [[decode-at-depth-after-p15]].

**The MoE prefill GEMM is bound by its per-tile slab unpack, not by rows.**
Measured four ways in P11 (row padding 1.90x → 1.19x is worth *nothing*; a
per-fragment bound, three sub-lists, and BM 128 all lose). So the way to speed
`moe.up` up is fewer tiles at the same block width = fewer experts touched = a
bigger ubatch. P12 adds the floor: **gutting the whole Q4_K scale path is only
1.21x**, and what remains after the loads are collected — an int→float
convert, an FMA and an f16 convert per weight — has **no bit-exact cheaper
form** (packed fp16 costs ~13 bits of mantissa; `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds toward
zero). At 21.1 TFLOP/s and 61 GB/s of bank it is neither matrix-core- nor
bandwidth-bound.

**What is measured dead (do not re-attempt without new information):**

- **Four arms on the gathered attention kernel, P14 (2026-09-22)**, and together
  they say what it is bound by. *Doubling the QK matrix work costs 2.7%*, so the
  matrix cores are ~5% of it. A subgroup staging barrier instead of a workgroup
  one is **1.00x**; staging two head-dim groups a barrier is **1.00x** and four
  is **0.75x**; putting two query heads in one workgroup so they share the staged
  key and value — which halves both the gather's global reads and its LDS writes
  — is **1.04x**, and four is **0.75x**. So it is not the matrix cores, not the
  barriers, not the gather's traffic and not occupancy-to-spare: what is left is
  the **LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head softmax scaffolding**,
  both of which scale with the union, which is why the kernel's cost is linear in
  the cells it visits. The 0.75x arms are LDS crowding out waves.
  `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP` and `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS` are the ladders, both at 1.

- **Compacting the live key blocks into a per-query-tile list is 1.00x at
  every depth** (P13, 2026-09-22) — it deletes 83% of the axis walk at 128k
  and `attn.attn` does not move. Third instance of the same rule, which is now
  the engine's and not any kernel's: *latency and redundant reads that matter
  at decode do not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy* — 3072
  single-wave workgroups against a decode step's 24. See
  [[long-context-prefill-128k]].

- **`hc.cn`'s 256-way reduction tree costs nothing** — deleting it outright is
  5331.5 µs against 5325.8. The non-bit-exact subgroup rewrite P11 queued
  would have bought zero.
- **`hc.cn`'s per-token gamma read costs nothing** — replacing it with a
  constant is 5332.9 µs. It is 40 KB and the MALL serves it. Its 57% of copy
  bandwidth is now *unexplained and out of hypotheses*.
- **Hoisting the attention block skip out of the loop is 1.00x at every
  depth.** At 64k a query tile skips ~1480 blocks, each on a dependent global
  read; voting on the whole key range up front with a subgroup ballot buys
  nothing, because **a prefill dispatches 3072 single-wave workgroups where a
  decode step dispatches 24** — latency that matters at decode does not matter
  at prefill, because prefill has occupancy. The exact converse of P8. **Still
  live for decode**, where it was deliberately never built.
- **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%** of the attention kernel, not the rest
  of the depth gap.

**At depth the fast loop is `-depth -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm**
([[long-context-prefill-128k]]) — `-attn` runs at `past = 0` and never
reaches depth's regime.

**`cmd/llm -attn` is the fast loop for attention at depth zero and it is 1.9 seconds** (two
layers, real routing, real selection, per-label µs a layer) — use it, not the
7-minute `-graph` ladder. It tops out near 16 384 tokens (32 768 in one batch
trips P0's watchdog) and runs at `past = 0`, so it reaches the selection's
regime but **not depth's**; only `-depth` does. `cmd/llm -moe` is the MoE's
equivalent at 228 ms to stage. See [[context-depth-rates]] for decode,
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]].

8	**Since L8a/L8b the dense banks are int8 rather than halves and residency is

14	is a ~2.0 s tail on top of staging. Without `LLM_DENSE_BANK` the run is still

17	**Do not schedule a whole-model run above ~2560 rows**: at 48 layers
18	`-graph -tokens 3072` (or `-ppl -ctx 4096`) **never returns** — it stalls
19	inside the driver's submit with one host thread at 100% and the GPU at 2-3%,
20	and the shim's 20 s fence timeout never fires, so it hangs indefinitely rather
21	than erroring. 2048 and 2560 are fine; the 4-layer prefix is fine at 4096.
22	This is a known open question in `research/llm-vertical.md`, not a mistake to re-discover.
23	
24	`go run ./cmd/llm -resident` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6a) stages every layer
25	of all five blocks: **84.20 GB of device buffers (82.40 since L8a), ~35 s wall
26	clock**, and it
27	ends with about 41 GB of MemAvailable left on this 117.7 GiB machine. Peak
28	host memory is separate — the dense blocks dequantise to f32 before packing,
29	and the 36 DeltaNet layers are 8.35 GB of transient floats at once — which is
30	why the tool stages dense first and the 77 GB expert bank last.
31	
32	**Why:** it is the only thing in the repo that takes most of the machine, so a
33	second GPU or large-allocation job started beside it will either fail to
34	allocate or perturb the timing it prints. `-bank N,N,...` restages just the
35	bank, which is the cheap way to vary residency; `-dense` is the 6.8 GB half

39	2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6b) are the same weight but **85.47 GB**, because they add

91	**The access log prints no bodies by default** (`-log-bodies` turns them back

139	**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
140	same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
141	measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel

151	So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
152	a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
153	binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
154	run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
155	logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
156	before any bitwise comparison.
157	
158	One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
159	MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
160	(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
161	`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
162	cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring

166	**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
167	*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
168	binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
169	kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.

192	name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
193	description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
194	metadata:
195	  type: project
196	---
197	
198	**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
199	`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
200	`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
201	to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
202	`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
203	flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
204	— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.
205	
206	Set it and staging is a disk read instead:
207	
208	    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache
209	
210	With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
211	71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
212	already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
213	(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
214	checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.
215	
216	**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
217	start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
218	wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
219	That part is unavoidable today.
220	
221	**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
222	is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
223	never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
224	resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
225	of a ~31 ms token.
226	
227	**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
228	sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
229	[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

239	
240	In `~/repos/strix-halo-vulkan` something outside the session commits the whole
241	working tree to `main` on a timer — the message is always `ai`, and the commits
242	land roughly every 30-45 minutes (observed 18:53, 19:37, 21:02, 21:36 on
243	2026-09-14). So a `git add -A && git commit` at the end of a session will often
244	print **"nothing to commit, working tree clean"** even though the work is
245	unsaved-looking: check `git show --stat HEAD` before concluding anything was
246	lost. There is an `origin` (github.com:theninj4/strix-halo-vulkan) but `main`
247	has **no upstream**, so nothing is pushed.
248	
249	**Other sessions edit this tree at the same time.** On 2026-09-18 a second
250	session was mid-refactor in `zimage/pipeline` and mid-write in `api/images.go`
251	while this one built `embed/`: `go build ./...` failed twice on *their*
252	undefined symbols (`p.latentH`, `formatSize`), minutes apart, and both cleared
253	on their own. Check `git status --short` and file mtimes before believing a
254	build break is yours, and build the packages you touched
255	(`go build ./embed/ ./api/ …`) rather than `./...` while it lasts.
256	
257	**Why:** the commit log is therefore not the project's narrative — `TODO.md`
258	is, and every session appends a handoff to it. That is why the repo's own docs
259	say to read `TODO.md`/the current vertical file first.
260	
261	**How to apply:** don't branch before committing here (the whole history is
262	direct-to-main), don't amend the `ai` commits to "improve" them, and put the
263	session's story in `TODO.md` rather than in a commit message. Edit files with
264	targeted replacements rather than whole-file rewrites when another session may
265	be in the same file, and never "fix" a symbol that belongs to their in-flight
266	work. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and [[phase-2-pivot-to-pipeline]] for what
267	the docs expect a session to record.

273	  type: project
274	---
275	
276	The `serve` binary runs as a **user** systemd unit, not a system one, and not
277	in the foreground:
278	
279	- **Install/redeploy: `./deploy.sh`.** It builds `./ai` from `./cmd/serve`,
280	  substitutes the unit's `###` placeholder with `$(pwd)`, writes
281	  `~/.config/systemd/user/ai.service`, `daemon-reload`s and restarts.
282	  `./ai.service` in the repo is a *template*, not a script — running it gives
283	  `Permission denied`, which is the expected outcome, not a bug to fix.
284	- **`deploy.sh` ends with `journalctl --user -n 100 -f -u ai`,** which never
285	  returns. In an agent session run its steps by hand and skip the tail.
286	- **Logs: `journalctl --user -u ai`** (`--user` is required; it is invisible to
287	  the system journal). The server logs one line per backend at startup and
288	  `listening on http://0.0.0.0:11434` when all of them are up.
289	- **Startup is ~25 s** and ~13 GB peak, nearly all of it the Z-Image backend;
290	  tts/stt/embed land in the first 3 s. Don't conclude anything from the log
291	  before the image line.
292	- **State without tailing:**
293	  `systemctl --user show ai.service -p ActiveState -p SubState -p NRestarts`.
294	  The unit ships `Restart=always` + `RestartSec=1`, and the server `log.Fatal`s
295	  on any bad flag or missing checkpoint, so a config mistake becomes a silent
296	  ~26 s crash loop. A non-zero `NRestarts` (or "restart counter is at N" in the
297	  journal) is the tell; `systemctl --user reset-failed ai.service` before a
298	  fixed redeploy so the count reads clean.
299	- **Auth: omitting `-token` does not disable it.** The flag *defaults* to a
300	  non-empty token (`defaultToken` in `cmd/serve/main.go`), so a unit that says
301	  nothing about tokens requires a bearer header on every `/v1` request. Only an
302	  explicitly empty `-token=` opens the server. This cost an afternoon once.
303	- **The deployed unit runs `-token=` on purpose**, chosen 2026-09-18: open, no
304	  bearer header, on `0.0.0.0:11434` so the second machine can reach it. Don't
305	  "fix" the empty token back to a default — it is the configuration that was
306	  asked for. See [[deployment-two-machines]].
307	- The unit is **`disabled`** as of 2026-09-18 — it does not come back on boot
308	  or login without `systemctl --user enable ai` and `loginctl enable-linger`.
309	
310	Anchor journal reads to the *current* instance
311	(`journalctl --user -u ai --since "@$(date -d "$(systemctl --user show
312	ai.service -p ExecMainStartTimestamp --value)" +%s)"`). A plain `--since -2min`
313	still contains the previous instance's crash lines and will make an
314	until-loop fire on a failure that is already fixed — the same self-matching
315	trap as [[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]]. See
316	[[deployment-two-machines]] for which box this is meant to run on and
317	[[gpu-debugging-access]] for when it hangs rather than exits.
318	
319	**The LLM line (P18, 2026-09-22)** is `-llm -llm-ctx 262144 -llm-batch 8192`: the full trained context, ~66 s and ~83 GB to come up. See [[llm-full-context-262k]].
320	---
321	name: never-edit-source-during-a-sweep
322	description: "`go run` rebuilds on every invocation, so editing repo source while a multi-arm benchmark script is running kills every arm after the one already in flight."
323	metadata:
324	  type: feedback
325	---
326	
327	**2026-09-21.** A four-arm 48-layer depth sweep lost three of its four arms.
328	The script called `go run ./cmd/llm` once per arm; arm 1 had already built and
329	ran fine; while it ran I edited `shaders/shaders.go` to add a new `//go:embed`
330	for a `.spv` that did not exist yet, and arms 2-4 each died instantly with
331	
332	    shaders/shaders.go:2646:12: pattern llm_attn_expand.spv: no matching files found
333	
334	~25 minutes of measurement, and the failure was silent in the sweep's own log
335	until the end.
336	
337	[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] already says "edit *text* while it runs, nothing
338	else" — that rule is about CPU contention perturbing the numbers. This is a
339	second, harder reason: **a multi-arm script that invokes `go run` rebuilds the
340	tree at the start of every arm**, so the source it compiles is whatever the
341	tree holds *then*, not what it held at launch. Even an edit that compiles
342	would silently measure a different binary in later arms, which is worse than
343	a crash.
344	
345	**How to apply:** make the benchmark script `go build -o <scratchpad>/bench
346	./cmd/llm` **once at the top** and run that binary for every arm. Then the
347	tree is free to edit while it runs, and every arm is provably the same build.
348	Select arms with environment variables read at dispatch time (this is what
349	`LLM_ATTN_SPLITS` and `LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS` are for), never by rebuilding.
350	---
351	name: prefill-rates
352	description: "Prompt-processing rates after P12 (2026-09-21), the ubatch curve and the decode cost that comes with it, what the MoE prefill GEMM is bound by, and the four prefill ideas that are measured dead."
353	metadata: 
354	  node_type: memory
355	  type: project
356	  originSessionId: d77f87a5-b722-4ac5-aaa9-d322f713f1da
357	  modified: 2026-09-21T22:34:23.069Z
358	---
359	
360	**Prefill does not plateau where llama.cpp's does, so the ubatch is a real
361	knob — but widening it is a trade, not a free win.** 48 layers, shipped banks,
362	two runs each (`results/p12_pp_*.csv`, write-ups `research/p11-prefill.md` and
363	`research/p12-prefill-round-two.md`):
364	
365	**Superseded at depth by P14 (2026-09-22)** — see [[long-context-prefill-128k]]
366	for the rates against context depth, which are no longer these. The depth-zero
367	ladder below stands.
368	
369	| ubatch | P11 | P12 | vs llama.cpp |
370	|---:|---:|---:|---:|
371	| 512 | 681.7 | 683.3 | 1.75x |
372	| 2048 | 1191.8 | **1207.7** | 3.08x |
373	| 4096 | 1340.7 | 1363.5 | 3.48x |
374	| 8192 | 1372.2 | **1403.9** | **3.59x** |
375	
376	Against **context depth** at ubatch 2048: 1154.6 / 968.1 / 894.3 / 805.7 /
377	**667.7** tok/s at 0 / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k. Arms are reproducible to
378	0.1-0.5%, so a 1.2% difference is real; quote means of two passes.
379	
380	**`-llm-batch` defaults to 4096 and, since P16 (2026-09-22), a wider batch
381	costs memory and nothing else.** P12-7 measured 4096 costing 8% of decode
382	through the server and P15 11-22% at depth; **that was a bug** — the DeltaNet
383	and attention input ports zero-padded a decode step out to the whole arena.
384	Fixed, through the server (four ~4k prompts, 256 generated, two passes to 0.1%):
385	
386	| batch | prefill | decode |
387	|---:|---:|---:|
388	| 2048 | 1052.2 | 34.19 |
389	| 4096 | 1198.5 | 34.20 |
390	| 8192 | 1232.5 | 34.16 |
391	
392	8192 only helps prompts > 4096 tokens, holds ~3 GB more, and lowers the
393	`maxStorageBufferRange` context cap. See [[decode-at-depth-after-p15]].
394	
395	**The MoE prefill GEMM is bound by its per-tile slab unpack, not by rows.**
396	Measured four ways in P11 (row padding 1.90x → 1.19x is worth *nothing*; a
397	per-fragment bound, three sub-lists, and BM 128 all lose). So the way to speed
398	`moe.up` up is fewer tiles at the same block width = fewer experts touched = a
399	bigger ubatch. P12 adds the floor: **gutting the whole Q4_K scale path is only
400	1.21x**, and what remains after the loads are collected — an int→float
401	convert, an FMA and an f16 convert per weight — has **no bit-exact cheaper
402	form** (packed fp16 costs ~13 bits of mantissa; `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds toward
403	zero). At 21.1 TFLOP/s and 61 GB/s of bank it is neither matrix-core- nor
404	bandwidth-bound.
405	
406	**What is measured dead (do not re-attempt without new information):**
407	
408	- **Four arms on the gathered attention kernel, P14 (2026-09-22)**, and together
409	  they say what it is bound by. *Doubling the QK matrix work costs 2.7%*, so the
410	  matrix cores are ~5% of it. A subgroup staging barrier instead of a workgroup
411	  one is **1.00x**; staging two head-dim groups a barrier is **1.00x** and four
412	  is **0.75x**; putting two query heads in one workgroup so they share the staged
413	  key and value — which halves both the gather's global reads and its LDS writes
414	  — is **1.04x**, and four is **0.75x**. So it is not the matrix cores, not the
415	  barriers, not the gather's traffic and not occupancy-to-spare: what is left is
416	  the **LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head softmax scaffolding**,
417	  both of which scale with the union, which is why the kernel's cost is linear in
418	  the cells it visits. The 0.75x arms are LDS crowding out waves.
419	  `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP` and `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS` are the ladders, both at 1.
420	
421	- **Compacting the live key blocks into a per-query-tile list is 1.00x at
422	  every depth** (P13, 2026-09-22) — it deletes 83% of the axis walk at 128k
423	  and `attn.attn` does not move. Third instance of the same rule, which is now
424	  the engine's and not any kernel's: *latency and redundant reads that matter
425	  at decode do not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy* — 3072
426	  single-wave workgroups against a decode step's 24. See
427	  [[long-context-prefill-128k]].
428	
429	- **`hc.cn`'s 256-way reduction tree costs nothing** — deleting it outright is
430	  5331.5 µs against 5325.8. The non-bit-exact subgroup rewrite P11 queued
431	  would have bought zero.
432	- **`hc.cn`'s per-token gamma read costs nothing** — replacing it with a
433	  constant is 5332.9 µs. It is 40 KB and the MALL serves it. Its 57% of copy
434	  bandwidth is now *unexplained and out of hypotheses*.
435	- **Hoisting the attention block skip out of the loop is 1.00x at every
436	  depth.** At 64k a query tile skips ~1480 blocks, each on a dependent global
437	  read; voting on the whole key range up front with a subgroup ballot buys
438	  nothing, because **a prefill dispatches 3072 single-wave workgroups where a
439	  decode step dispatches 24** — latency that matters at decode does not matter
440	  at prefill, because prefill has occupancy. The exact converse of P8. **Still
441	  live for decode**, where it was deliberately never built.
442	- **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%** of the attention kernel, not the rest
443	  of the depth gap.
444	
445	**At depth the fast loop is `-depth -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm**
446	([[long-context-prefill-128k]]) — `-attn` runs at `past = 0` and never
447	reaches depth's regime.
448	
449	**`cmd/llm -attn` is the fast loop for attention at depth zero and it is 1.9 seconds** (two
450	layers, real routing, real selection, per-label µs a layer) — use it, not the
451	7-minute `-graph` ladder. It tops out near 16 384 tokens (32 768 in one batch
452	trips P0's watchdog) and runs at `past = 0`, so it reaches the selection's
453	regime but **not depth's**; only `-depth` does. `cmd/llm -moe` is the MoE's
454	equivalent at 228 ms to stage. See [[context-depth-rates]] for decode,
455	[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
456	[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]].
457	---
458	name: long-context-prefill-128k
459	description: "Prefill against depth out to 128k: P17 (2026-09-22) takes it to 1011 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 1176 at 4096 with heads on the fragment rows; P14's four changes, refusals and the fast 4-layer probe below."
460	metadata: 
461	  node_type: memory
462	  type: project
463	  originSessionId: 80f71c47-a621-4724-a77a-e285f8d84b61
464	  modified: 2026-09-22T11:38:44.739Z
465	---
466	
467	**Superseded by P17 (2026-09-22, `research/p17-heads-on-rows.md`): 128k
468	prefills at 1011.4 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 1175.7 at the served 4096** (from
469	833.5 / 899.7), 64k 1048.6 → 1081 with P17-2. P17-1 puts a token's 12 query
470	heads (one kv head) on the fragment's M rows, so the gathered list is one
471	token's 2051 cells, not a 16-token union of 7049, and the mask pass is gone
472	(`attn.attn` 3.25x). Taken for prefill at `past >= selWidth` and always at
473	decode, where it is bit-identical. P17-2 `Graph.PrefetchPLE` faults the
474	next chunk's n-gram pages in while the GPU runs this one (+3.1% at depth).
475	Knobs: `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS=0|1` (1 *forces* it, bypassing the depth rule —
476	an A/B with =1 measures depth 0 wrong), `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS_MIN`,
477	`LLM_PLE_PREFETCH=0`. Gate: `TestAttnGPUHeadRowsIsTheGather`. The union
478	"floor" P14 called unclosable below was closed by changing what the rows are.
479	
480	**P14's text, for its four changes:** 128 000 cells prefilled at 826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946.1 at
481	8192 — `GOALS.md`'s 900 is met. P13 left it at 563.6. 48 layers, shipped banks,
482	`wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward, `-tg 8 -ctx 139000`. Write-up
483	`research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md`.
484	
485	| depth | P13 pp | P14 pp | | decode |
486	|------:|-------:|-------:|----:|-------:|
487	| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.31 |
488	| 32 000 | 825.8 | 915.6 | 1.11x | 25.80 |
489	| 64 000 | 719.6 | 892.1 | 1.24x | 24.46 |
490	| 96 000 | 607.9 | 832.3 | 1.37x | 22.80 |
491	| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.18 |
492	
493	Falloff from depth zero **0.50x → 0.72x**. Against the ubatch at 128 000 alone
494	(two runs each): 826.0 at 2048, 886.1 at 4096 (the shipped
495	`-llm-batch`), **946.1 at 8192** — P12's trade at depth, so 8192 is a
496	batch summariser's setting. **Decode is the control and did not move.**
497	
498	**Four changes.**
499	
500	1. **The selection runs over block scores, not the expanded per-cell tensor**
501	   (`llm_attn_selblk.comp`). All `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score,
502	   so a weighted select over `nKV/ratio` entries is the same threshold, ties and
503	   bitmask. `attn.select` 0.281 → **0.020** (13.8x), `attn.expand` deleted, and
504	   **1.14 GB of arena** freed at ubatch 2048. Bit-identical, gated by
505	   `TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect` over four chunk schedules.
506	2. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather** (`llm_attn_gather.comp` +
507	   `llm_attn_wmma.comp -DGATHER`). Per query tile, the union of its rows'
508	   selections compacted ascending, with the causal test folded into a per-row
509	   mask over the gathered positions. `attn.attn` 1.024 → **0.454** (2.15x on the
510	   4-layer probe; 0.566 → 0.303 at 48 layers). **The value plane had to become
511	   cell-major first** — a selected run is `ratio` consecutive cells, one
512	   128-byte line, where transposed it was four halves out of sixteen rows. That
513	   costs the block kernel ~7% and decode nothing.
514	3. **The indexer's score on the matrix cores** (`llm_attn_score_wmma.comp`). It
515	   is a GEMM per indexer head with a rectifier: 0.077 → **0.034**. Chunk-invariant
516	   (a matrix product's rows are independent), and *nearer* llama.cpp's selection
517	   than the scalar kernel (9760 vs 9762 of 6 298 621).
518	4. **`checkBufferRange`** — see [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]].
519	
520	**The gather is the first kernel here that is not chunk-invariant and cannot be
521	made so.** Its list is the union of a query tile's sixteen rows, so a chunk
522	ending inside the tile gathers a different list and the online softmax folds the
523	same terms in a different order. It is off under `Graph.PinSchedule` with the
524	other reassociating kernels, and the chunk-equality gates pin it (`SetGather`).
525	A prompt prefilled twice at the same ubatch is still bit-identical; only changing
526	the ubatch moves the last places. Gates: `TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells`
527	(exact on the set), `TestAttnGPUGatherIsTheBlockKernel` (4.1e-06 rms against
528	9.9e-04 from llama.cpp), `TestAttnGPUGatherRungsAgree`,
529	`TestAttnGPUGatherIsDispatched`.
530	
531	**The union is the number that prices all of this, and P13's estimate of it was
532	wrong.** `AttnGPU.SelUnion` measures it: at 128 000 cells a 16-row tile reads
533	**15 145** cells where its rows' union is **7 049** and one row selects 2 051.
534	The gather is therefore 2.15x, not the 3.3x P13 projected, and the 3.4x between
535	the union and one row is the floor a 16-row fragment cannot reach.
536	
537	**What the gathered kernel is bound by, by elimination** — four arms, all
538	1.00x-ish, in [[prefill-rates]]: not the matrix cores (doubling their work costs
539	2.7%), not the barriers, not the gather's own traffic (sharing it across two
540	heads buys 4%). It is the LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head
541	softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union.
542	
543	**The fast loop is still `-depth ... -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm** — and it
544	**overstates** `attn.attn` because its one attention layer is denser than the
545	48-layer mean (19.0% live at bm16/bn16 against 11.7%). Ratios reproduce;
546	absolutes do not.
547	
548	    /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4
549	
550	**Control arms**: `LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_KERNEL=qt1_kt1|qt1_kt4`,
551	`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS`, `LLM_ATTN_EXPAND_CELLS=1` (also
552	what `Cells()` needs), `LLM_ATTN_SCORE=scalar`.
553	
554	**The whole-model check.** Three of the four changes claim bit-exactness, and
555	`TestGraphLogits` confirms all three at once: its diagnostics come back
556	byte-identical to the base (`maxAbs 2.507e+00 at 141557`, `rms 5.148e-01`, the
557	same top ten) through all 48 layers. Its *failure* is the pre-existing one — see
558	[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]], and note that a relative `LLM_BANK_CACHE` there
559	writes 23 GB into `llm/models`, which this session walked into.
560	
561	See [[prefill-rates]], [[context-depth-rates]], [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]],
562	[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
563	[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[graphstats-kinds-aliases]].
