---
name: llm-resident-run
description: The whole-model runs (`cmd/llm -resident`, `-graph`, `-gen`, `-ppl`, `cmd/serve -llm`, `TestGraphLogits`) stage 82-83 GB of qwen3.8-flash-next; what they cost in time and RAM, and why nothing else can run beside them.
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Since L8a/L8b the dense banks are int8 rather than halves and residency is
81.89 GB with the head** (`-dense` 4.32 GB); `LLM_DENSE_FP16=1` puts every
block back on the old halves and restores the old sizes exactly, which is how
the two are compared. **A decode token is 31.7 ms and residency 79.85 GB as of
L8c-7 (2026-09-17)** with all five 4.5-bit families named in
`LLM_DENSE_BANK` — 40.5 ms at L8e, 33.3 at L8c-6, ~134 before L7d — so `-n 64`
is a ~2.0 s tail on top of staging. Without `LLM_DENSE_BANK` the run is still
L8a's int8 bank at 81.89 GB and 40.5 ms.

**Do not schedule a whole-model run above ~2560 rows**: at 48 layers
`-graph -tokens 3072` (or `-ppl -ctx 4096`) **never returns** — it stalls
inside the driver's submit with one host thread at 100% and the GPU at 2-3%,
and the shim's 20 s fence timeout never fires, so it hangs indefinitely rather
than erroring. 2048 and 2560 are fine; the 4-layer prefix is fine at 4096.
This is a known open question in `research/llm-vertical.md`, not a mistake to re-discover.

`go run ./cmd/llm -resident` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6a) stages every layer
of all five blocks: **84.20 GB of device buffers (82.40 since L8a), ~35 s wall
clock**, and it
ends with about 41 GB of MemAvailable left on this 117.7 GiB machine. Peak
host memory is separate — the dense blocks dequantise to f32 before packing,
and the 36 DeltaNet layers are 8.35 GB of transient floats at once — which is
why the tool stages dense first and the 77 GB expert bank last.

**Why:** it is the only thing in the repo that takes most of the machine, so a
second GPU or large-allocation job started beside it will either fail to
allocate or perturb the timing it prints. `-bank N,N,...` restages just the
bank, which is the cheap way to vary residency; `-dense` is the 6.8 GB half
and runs in 8 s.

`go run ./cmd/llm -graph` and `go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphLogits` (added
2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6b) are the same weight but **85.47 GB**, because they add
the 1.27 GB lm head; `-tokens 2048` adds another ~1.1 GB of arenas. Staging is
~35-40 s, so budget a 1800 s timeout. Both take a `-layers 4` / `GraphOpts{
Layers: 4}` prefix that is 7.4 GB and three seconds — use that while changing
anything about the order, and the full stage only for the gate.

`go run ./cmd/llm -gen` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L7c) is the same 85.47 GB
plus the KV cache, and it is the slow one: staging is ~35-50 s and generation
is **~40.5 ms a token** (see above), so `-n 64` is a ~2.6 s tail on top.
**Every committed decode CSV is `-prompt 'The capital of France is'`**; the
flag's default is the 81-token `graphDefaultPrompt`, on which the model emits
EOS at the first step and the decode row is meaningless. A 900 s timeout
covers `-n 64`; a two-minute one does not even cover the staging. `-layers 4`
is 7.4 GB, ~2 s to stage and ~18 ms a token, which is the right thing to use
for anything about the loop rather than about the rate.

`go run ./cmd/llm -ppl` (added 2026-09-17, research/llm-vertical.md L8c-0) is the longest of
them: 81.89 GB, ~37 s of staging and then **3.3 s per 2048-token chunk for 145
chunks — 7m58s** over `wiki.test.raw`, so run it in the background and wait on
the log rather than holding a foreground timeout. `-chunks N` cuts it (4
chunks is ~15 s after staging) but **only screens for broken**: four chunks
read +0.32% against llama.cpp where the whole corpus reads −0.13%, sign and
all. `-layers 4` plus `-chunks 2` is the 8 GB plumbing check. The reference
side is `llama-perplexity -c 2048 -b 2048`, ~6.5 s a chunk, and it needs the
machine too — never both at once. **`LLM_DENSE_SIM=<plan>` forces the fp16
arm** (L8c-1), so a simulated run is the old 84 GB residency and ~6 s longer
to stage, and its tok/s means nothing — it grades accuracy only.
`LLM_DENSE_SIM_QUANT=imatrix` needs `models/…/imatrix_unsloth.gguf` (the
fetch script gets it; note the source's `_file` suffix) and adds ~10 s of
staging for the nineteen-rung scale search.

**Since P4b/D20 (2026-09-19) a served-default run also stages the MoE bank
narrower, and it is not free at startup.** `LLM_MOE_BANK` (default off in
`cmd/llm`, set to `llm.ShippedMoEBank` by `cmd/serve -llm`) transcodes four
tensor families out of the checkpoint's bytes — 4.2 B weights of
`ffn_down_exps` plus 236 M of the shared expert — so **the MoE block stages
in ~52 s instead of ~25**, and a whole-model run is ~1m32s to first chunk
rather than ~40 s. Residency drops 77.41 -> 76.00 GB in that block (78.53 GB
whole-model with D19's dense bank). Budget the extra minute in every timeout;
`LLM_MOE_BANK=off` is the control.

`go run ./cmd/serve -llm` (added 2026-09-17, research/llm-vertical.md L9a) is the same residency
held open: **33.5 s to stage at `-llm-ctx 4096`**, ~84 GB, and it then serves
until interrupted. A request is a prefill plus ~44 ms a token (22.7 tok/s
through the server on the L8 banks), so a 48-token answer is under a second.
Start it in the background, poll the log for `listening on`, and **kill it
with `pkill -f '[e]xe/serve'` when finished** — the bracket matters, because
`pkill -f 'exe/serve'` matches the shell running it and kills the session
instead (the same trap as [[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]]). It holds
the machine for as long as it runs. `-llm-layers 4` is the 7 GB, 3.5 s prefix
and is the right thing for anything about HTTP rather than about the text.

**The access log prints no bodies by default** (`-log-bodies` turns them back
on): a chat server's bodies are conversations. The per-request `llm:` line is
separate and always printed — prompt tokens, how many were reused from the
last turn, and the two rates.

**The model path must name a shard, not the directory.**
`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/` now holds three checkpoints — the model, the
imatrix and the MTP head — so `gguf.OpenSet` refuses it as ambiguous and
`cmd/llm`'s own `-model` default no longer resolves. Pass
`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf`,
which is what `cmd/serve` defaults to.

**`-layers 24` is the end-to-end instrument when 48 will not fit.** With the
`ai` user service resident (~7 GB) this machine has ~80 GB MemAvailable
against a 48-layer `-graph`'s ~80 GB, which is too tight to schedule. A
24-layer `-graph` is **~40 GB, ~2 min to first number**, and it is a *real*
whole-graph measurement — all five blocks, the head, the host loop, the
per-block ms columns in the CSV — not a block bench. Its one distortion is
that the M-independent fixed costs (head 2.4 ms, `ple`, `move`, host) are 24%
of a step there against 13% at 48 layers, so any *ratio* read off it is
optimistic and the 48-layer number is owed (P5, 2026-09-19).

**How to apply:** run them in the foreground with a long timeout and nothing
else on the GPU, the way [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] asks. `-resident`'s closing
measurement (layer 3's MoE block) is comparable to `-moe -tokens 512 -iters 10`
only at the same iteration count.
---
name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a
`-gen` run cost one control pass 1.6 tok/s of 35 (P4c, 2026-09-19), which is
four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].
---
name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.

Set it and staging is a disk read instead:

    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache

With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.

**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
That part is unavoidable today.

**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
of a ~31 ms token.

**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].
---
name: auto-committer-owns-main
description: "An external process auto-commits the strix-halo-vulkan working tree to main every ~30-45 min with the message \"ai\", and other sessions edit the same tree concurrently, so `go build ./...` can fail on someone else's half-written file."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8382387e-ec90-4d7d-8642-1d65b8bbd10a
  modified: 2026-09-17T23:25:30.192Z
---

In `~/repos/strix-halo-vulkan` something outside the session commits the whole
working tree to `main` on a timer — the message is always `ai`, and the commits
land roughly every 30-45 minutes (observed 18:53, 19:37, 21:02, 21:36 on
2026-09-14). So a `git add -A && git commit` at the end of a session will often
print **"nothing to commit, working tree clean"** even though the work is
unsaved-looking: check `git show --stat HEAD` before concluding anything was
lost. There is an `origin` (github.com:theninj4/strix-halo-vulkan) but `main`
has **no upstream**, so nothing is pushed.

**Other sessions edit this tree at the same time.** On 2026-09-18 a second
session was mid-refactor in `zimage/pipeline` and mid-write in `api/images.go`
while this one built `embed/`: `go build ./...` failed twice on *their*
undefined symbols (`p.latentH`, `formatSize`), minutes apart, and both cleared
on their own. Check `git status --short` and file mtimes before believing a
build break is yours, and build the packages you touched
(`go build ./embed/ ./api/ …`) rather than `./...` while it lasts.

**Why:** the commit log is therefore not the project's narrative — `TODO.md`
is, and every session appends a handoff to it. That is why the repo's own docs
say to read `TODO.md`/the current vertical file first.

**How to apply:** don't branch before committing here (the whole history is
direct-to-main), don't amend the `ai` commits to "improve" them, and put the
session's story in `TODO.md` rather than in a commit message. Edit files with
targeted replacements rather than whole-file rewrites when another session may
be in the same file, and never "fix" a symbol that belongs to their in-flight
work. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and [[phase-2-pivot-to-pipeline]] for what
the docs expect a session to record.
---
name: ai-service-user-unit
description: "The ai server runs as a --user systemd unit on :11434; logs are journalctl --user -u ai, deploy.sh installs it, startup takes ~25 s, and it is deliberately served open with -token=."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

The `serve` binary runs as a **user** systemd unit, not a system one, and not
in the foreground:

- **Install/redeploy: `./deploy.sh`.** It builds `./ai` from `./cmd/serve`,
  substitutes the unit's `###` placeholder with `$(pwd)`, writes
  `~/.config/systemd/user/ai.service`, `daemon-reload`s and restarts.
  `./ai.service` in the repo is a *template*, not a script — running it gives
  `Permission denied`, which is the expected outcome, not a bug to fix.
- **`deploy.sh` ends with `journalctl --user -n 100 -f -u ai`,** which never
  returns. In an agent session run its steps by hand and skip the tail.
- **Logs: `journalctl --user -u ai`** (`--user` is required; it is invisible to
  the system journal). The server logs one line per backend at startup and
  `listening on http://0.0.0.0:11434` when all of them are up.
- **Startup is ~25 s** and ~13 GB peak, nearly all of it the Z-Image backend;
  tts/stt/embed land in the first 3 s. Don't conclude anything from the log
  before the image line.
- **State without tailing:**
  `systemctl --user show ai.service -p ActiveState -p SubState -p NRestarts`.
  The unit ships `Restart=always` + `RestartSec=1`, and the server `log.Fatal`s
  on any bad flag or missing checkpoint, so a config mistake becomes a silent
  ~26 s crash loop. A non-zero `NRestarts` (or "restart counter is at N" in the
  journal) is the tell; `systemctl --user reset-failed ai.service` before a
  fixed redeploy so the count reads clean.
- **Auth: omitting `-token` does not disable it.** The flag *defaults* to a
  non-empty token (`defaultToken` in `cmd/serve/main.go`), so a unit that says
  nothing about tokens requires a bearer header on every `/v1` request. Only an
  explicitly empty `-token=` opens the server. This cost an afternoon once.
- **The deployed unit runs `-token=` on purpose**, chosen 2026-09-18: open, no
  bearer header, on `0.0.0.0:11434` so the second machine can reach it. Don't
  "fix" the empty token back to a default — it is the configuration that was
  asked for. See [[deployment-two-machines]].
- The unit is **`disabled`** as of 2026-09-18 — it does not come back on boot
  or login without `systemctl --user enable ai` and `loginctl enable-linger`.

Anchor journal reads to the *current* instance
(`journalctl --user -u ai --since "@$(date -d "$(systemctl --user show
ai.service -p ExecMainStartTimestamp --value)" +%s)"`). A plain `--since -2min`
still contains the previous instance's crash lines and will make an
until-loop fire on a failure that is already fixed — the same self-matching
trap as [[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]]. See
[[deployment-two-machines]] for which box this is meant to run on and
[[gpu-debugging-access]] for when it hangs rather than exits.

**The LLM line (P18, 2026-09-22)** is `-llm -llm-ctx 262144 -llm-batch 8192`: the full trained context, ~66 s and ~83 GB to come up. See [[llm-full-context-262k]].
---
name: never-edit-source-during-a-sweep
description: "`go run` rebuilds on every invocation, so editing repo source while a multi-arm benchmark script is running kills every arm after the one already in flight."
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

**2026-09-21.** A four-arm 48-layer depth sweep lost three of its four arms.
The script called `go run ./cmd/llm` once per arm; arm 1 had already built and
ran fine; while it ran I edited `shaders/shaders.go` to add a new `//go:embed`
for a `.spv` that did not exist yet, and arms 2-4 each died instantly with

    shaders/shaders.go:2646:12: pattern llm_attn_expand.spv: no matching files found

~25 minutes of measurement, and the failure was silent in the sweep's own log
until the end.

[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] already says "edit *text* while it runs, nothing
else" — that rule is about CPU contention perturbing the numbers. This is a
second, harder reason: **a multi-arm script that invokes `go run` rebuilds the
tree at the start of every arm**, so the source it compiles is whatever the
tree holds *then*, not what it held at launch. Even an edit that compiles
would silently measure a different binary in later arms, which is worse than
a crash.

**How to apply:** make the benchmark script `go build -o <scratchpad>/bench
./cmd/llm` **once at the top** and run that binary for every arm. Then the
tree is free to edit while it runs, and every arm is provably the same build.
Select arms with environment variables read at dispatch time (this is what
`LLM_ATTN_SPLITS` and `LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS` are for), never by rebuilding.
---
name: prefill-rates
description: "Prompt-processing rates after P12 (2026-09-21), the ubatch curve and the decode cost that comes with it, what the MoE prefill GEMM is bound by, and the four prefill ideas that are measured dead."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d77f87a5-b722-4ac5-aaa9-d322f713f1da
  modified: 2026-09-21T22:34:23.069Z
---

**Prefill does not plateau where llama.cpp's does, so the ubatch is a real
knob — but widening it is a trade, not a free win.** 48 layers, shipped banks,
two runs each (`results/p12_pp_*.csv`, write-ups `research/p11-prefill.md` and
`research/p12-prefill-round-two.md`):

**Superseded at depth by P14 (2026-09-22)** — see [[long-context-prefill-128k]]
for the rates against context depth, which are no longer these. The depth-zero
ladder below stands.

| ubatch | P11 | P12 | vs llama.cpp |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 681.7 | 683.3 | 1.75x |
| 2048 | 1191.8 | **1207.7** | 3.08x |
| 4096 | 1340.7 | 1363.5 | 3.48x |
| 8192 | 1372.2 | **1403.9** | **3.59x** |

Against **context depth** at ubatch 2048: 1154.6 / 968.1 / 894.3 / 805.7 /
**667.7** tok/s at 0 / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k. Arms are reproducible to
0.1-0.5%, so a 1.2% difference is real; quote means of two passes.

**`-llm-batch` defaults to 4096 and, since P16 (2026-09-22), a wider batch
costs memory and nothing else.** P12-7 measured 4096 costing 8% of decode
through the server and P15 11-22% at depth; **that was a bug** — the DeltaNet
and attention input ports zero-padded a decode step out to the whole arena.
Fixed, through the server (four ~4k prompts, 256 generated, two passes to 0.1%):

| batch | prefill | decode |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 1052.2 | 34.19 |
| 4096 | 1198.5 | 34.20 |
| 8192 | 1232.5 | 34.16 |

8192 only helps prompts > 4096 tokens, holds ~3 GB more, and lowers the
`maxStorageBufferRange` context cap. See [[decode-at-depth-after-p15]].

**The MoE prefill GEMM is bound by its per-tile slab unpack, not by rows.**
Measured four ways in P11 (row padding 1.90x → 1.19x is worth *nothing*; a
per-fragment bound, three sub-lists, and BM 128 all lose). So the way to speed
`moe.up` up is fewer tiles at the same block width = fewer experts touched = a
bigger ubatch. P12 adds the floor: **gutting the whole Q4_K scale path is only
1.21x**, and what remains after the loads are collected — an int→float
convert, an FMA and an f16 convert per weight — has **no bit-exact cheaper
form** (packed fp16 costs ~13 bits of mantissa; `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds toward
zero). At 21.1 TFLOP/s and 61 GB/s of bank it is neither matrix-core- nor
bandwidth-bound.

**What is measured dead (do not re-attempt without new information):**

- **Four arms on the gathered attention kernel, P14 (2026-09-22)**, and together
  they say what it is bound by. *Doubling the QK matrix work costs 2.7%*, so the
  matrix cores are ~5% of it. A subgroup staging barrier instead of a workgroup
  one is **1.00x**; staging two head-dim groups a barrier is **1.00x** and four
  is **0.75x**; putting two query heads in one workgroup so they share the staged
  key and value — which halves both the gather's global reads and its LDS writes
  — is **1.04x**, and four is **0.75x**. So it is not the matrix cores, not the
  barriers, not the gather's traffic and not occupancy-to-spare: what is left is
  the **LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head softmax scaffolding**,
  both of which scale with the union, which is why the kernel's cost is linear in
  the cells it visits. The 0.75x arms are LDS crowding out waves.
  `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP` and `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS` are the ladders, both at 1.

- **Compacting the live key blocks into a per-query-tile list is 1.00x at
  every depth** (P13, 2026-09-22) — it deletes 83% of the axis walk at 128k
  and `attn.attn` does not move. Third instance of the same rule, which is now
  the engine's and not any kernel's: *latency and redundant reads that matter
  at decode do not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy* — 3072
  single-wave workgroups against a decode step's 24. See
  [[long-context-prefill-128k]].

- **`hc.cn`'s 256-way reduction tree costs nothing** — deleting it outright is
  5331.5 µs against 5325.8. The non-bit-exact subgroup rewrite P11 queued
  would have bought zero.
- **`hc.cn`'s per-token gamma read costs nothing** — replacing it with a
  constant is 5332.9 µs. It is 40 KB and the MALL serves it. Its 57% of copy
  bandwidth is now *unexplained and out of hypotheses*.
- **Hoisting the attention block skip out of the loop is 1.00x at every
  depth.** At 64k a query tile skips ~1480 blocks, each on a dependent global
  read; voting on the whole key range up front with a subgroup ballot buys
  nothing, because **a prefill dispatches 3072 single-wave workgroups where a
  decode step dispatches 24** — latency that matters at decode does not matter
  at prefill, because prefill has occupancy. The exact converse of P8. **Still
  live for decode**, where it was deliberately never built.
- **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%** of the attention kernel, not the rest
  of the depth gap.

**At depth the fast loop is `-depth -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm**
([[long-context-prefill-128k]]) — `-attn` runs at `past = 0` and never
reaches depth's regime.

**`cmd/llm -attn` is the fast loop for attention at depth zero and it is 1.9 seconds** (two
layers, real routing, real selection, per-label µs a layer) — use it, not the
7-minute `-graph` ladder. It tops out near 16 384 tokens (32 768 in one batch
trips P0's watchdog) and runs at `past = 0`, so it reaches the selection's
regime but **not depth's**; only `-depth` does. `cmd/llm -moe` is the MoE's
equivalent at 228 ms to stage. See [[context-depth-rates]] for decode,
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]].
---
name: long-context-prefill-128k
description: "Prefill against depth out to 128k: P17 (2026-09-22) takes it to 1011 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 1176 at 4096 with heads on the fragment rows; P14's four changes, refusals and the fast 4-layer probe below."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 80f71c47-a621-4724-a77a-e285f8d84b61
  modified: 2026-09-22T11:38:44.739Z
---

**Superseded by P17 (2026-09-22, `research/p17-heads-on-rows.md`): 128k
prefills at 1011.4 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 1175.7 at the served 4096** (from
833.5 / 899.7), 64k 1048.6 → 1081 with P17-2. P17-1 puts a token's 12 query
heads (one kv head) on the fragment's M rows, so the gathered list is one
token's 2051 cells, not a 16-token union of 7049, and the mask pass is gone
(`attn.attn` 3.25x). Taken for prefill at `past >= selWidth` and always at
decode, where it is bit-identical. P17-2 `Graph.PrefetchPLE` faults the
next chunk's n-gram pages in while the GPU runs this one (+3.1% at depth).
Knobs: `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS=0|1` (1 *forces* it, bypassing the depth rule —
an A/B with =1 measures depth 0 wrong), `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS_MIN`,
`LLM_PLE_PREFETCH=0`. Gate: `TestAttnGPUHeadRowsIsTheGather`. The union
"floor" P14 called unclosable below was closed by changing what the rows are.

**P14's text, for its four changes:** 128 000 cells prefilled at 826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946.1 at
8192 — `GOALS.md`'s 900 is met. P13 left it at 563.6. 48 layers, shipped banks,
`wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward, `-tg 8 -ctx 139000`. Write-up
`research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md`.

| depth | P13 pp | P14 pp | | decode |
|------:|-------:|-------:|----:|-------:|
| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.31 |
| 32 000 | 825.8 | 915.6 | 1.11x | 25.80 |
| 64 000 | 719.6 | 892.1 | 1.24x | 24.46 |
| 96 000 | 607.9 | 832.3 | 1.37x | 22.80 |
| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.18 |

Falloff from depth zero **0.50x → 0.72x**. Against the ubatch at 128 000 alone
(two runs each): 826.0 at 2048, 886.1 at 4096 (the shipped
`-llm-batch`), **946.1 at 8192** — P12's trade at depth, so 8192 is a
batch summariser's setting. **Decode is the control and did not move.**

**Four changes.**

1. **The selection runs over block scores, not the expanded per-cell tensor**
   (`llm_attn_selblk.comp`). All `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score,
   so a weighted select over `nKV/ratio` entries is the same threshold, ties and
   bitmask. `attn.select` 0.281 → **0.020** (13.8x), `attn.expand` deleted, and
   **1.14 GB of arena** freed at ubatch 2048. Bit-identical, gated by
   `TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect` over four chunk schedules.
2. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather** (`llm_attn_gather.comp` +
   `llm_attn_wmma.comp -DGATHER`). Per query tile, the union of its rows'
   selections compacted ascending, with the causal test folded into a per-row
   mask over the gathered positions. `attn.attn` 1.024 → **0.454** (2.15x on the
   4-layer probe; 0.566 → 0.303 at 48 layers). **The value plane had to become
   cell-major first** — a selected run is `ratio` consecutive cells, one
   128-byte line, where transposed it was four halves out of sixteen rows. That
   costs the block kernel ~7% and decode nothing.
3. **The indexer's score on the matrix cores** (`llm_attn_score_wmma.comp`). It
   is a GEMM per indexer head with a rectifier: 0.077 → **0.034**. Chunk-invariant
   (a matrix product's rows are independent), and *nearer* llama.cpp's selection
   than the scalar kernel (9760 vs 9762 of 6 298 621).
4. **`checkBufferRange`** — see [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]].

**The gather is the first kernel here that is not chunk-invariant and cannot be
made so.** Its list is the union of a query tile's sixteen rows, so a chunk
ending inside the tile gathers a different list and the online softmax folds the
same terms in a different order. It is off under `Graph.PinSchedule` with the
other reassociating kernels, and the chunk-equality gates pin it (`SetGather`).
A prompt prefilled twice at the same ubatch is still bit-identical; only changing
the ubatch moves the last places. Gates: `TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells`
(exact on the set), `TestAttnGPUGatherIsTheBlockKernel` (4.1e-06 rms against
9.9e-04 from llama.cpp), `TestAttnGPUGatherRungsAgree`,
`TestAttnGPUGatherIsDispatched`.

**The union is the number that prices all of this, and P13's estimate of it was
wrong.** `AttnGPU.SelUnion` measures it: at 128 000 cells a 16-row tile reads
**15 145** cells where its rows' union is **7 049** and one row selects 2 051.
The gather is therefore 2.15x, not the 3.3x P13 projected, and the 3.4x between
the union and one row is the floor a 16-row fragment cannot reach.

**What the gathered kernel is bound by, by elimination** — four arms, all
1.00x-ish, in [[prefill-rates]]: not the matrix cores (doubling their work costs
2.7%), not the barriers, not the gather's own traffic (sharing it across two
heads buys 4%). It is the LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head
softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union.

**The fast loop is still `-depth ... -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm** — and it
**overstates** `attn.attn` because its one attention layer is denser than the
48-layer mean (19.0% live at bm16/bn16 against 11.7%). Ratios reproduce;
absolutes do not.

    /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4

**Control arms**: `LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_KERNEL=qt1_kt1|qt1_kt4`,
`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS`, `LLM_ATTN_EXPAND_CELLS=1` (also
what `Cells()` needs), `LLM_ATTN_SCORE=scalar`.

**The whole-model check.** Three of the four changes claim bit-exactness, and
`TestGraphLogits` confirms all three at once: its diagnostics come back
byte-identical to the base (`maxAbs 2.507e+00 at 141557`, `rms 5.148e-01`, the
same top ten) through all 48 layers. Its *failure* is the pre-existing one — see
[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]], and note that a relative `LLM_BANK_CACHE` there
writes 23 GB into `llm/models`, which this session walked into.

See [[prefill-rates]], [[context-depth-rates]], [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]],
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[graphstats-kinds-aliases]].

content.content:
---
name: llm-test-suite-gotchas
description: "Three ways go test ./llm/ misleads: Go's 10-minute default timeout, a TestGraphLogits failure that is pre-existing on main, and a relative LLM_BANK_CACHE writing 23 GB into llm/."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d77f87a5-b722-4ac5-aaa9-d322f713f1da
  modified: 2026-09-21T22:34:36.040Z
---

**`go test ./llm/` needs `-timeout 60m`.** Go's default is ten minutes and the
suite runs past it inside `TestQSASelectionSurvivesOurScores`. What you get is
a panic stack and `FAIL strix-halo-vulkan/llm 600.024s`, which **reads as a
real failure and is not one**. With a warm bank cache the whole suite is

`go run ./cmd/llm -spec` (added 2026-09-19, P5c) stages the 48-layer trunk
**and** the 1.92 GB draft head and then runs two arms interleaved in one
process — a plain greedy loop and the speculative one — because P1c's
environment finding means a decode rate from a different day is not a control.
**~85 GB, ~31 s to stage the trunk plus ~1 s for the draft, then ~5 s per
128-token arm**; `-spec-passes 2` (the default) is four arms, so budget ~1200 s
and pass the shard path, not the directory (see [[llm-resident-run]]).

- `-ctx 512` is the short arm; `-spec-prefix N` prompts with the first N tokens
  of `-ppl-file` instead of `-prompt`, which is the long arm. **Never above
  `-ctx 2048`** — the draft head refuses, for the reason in
  [[mtp-draft-head-run]].
- `-layers 4` is the 9 GB plumbing check: the mechanics work and the
  acceptance rate is 0%, because the draft head was trained against 48 layers.
- `SPEC_PLAIN_ONLY=1` drops the speculative arm and runs the plain loop
  against itself. It is the control on the control and it is not optional.

**Two things to read before quoting a multiplier.**

1. **The pairwise id table, including the plain-against-plain rows.** At the

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. 540:**Two costs, and neither is C6's:**
541-- **The 237k prefill runs at 901 tok/s, against P18's ~1022.** With more
542-  than one slot a background prefill is cut into `-llm-preempt-chunk` (2048)
543-  chunks, and at this length that is ~116 chunks of C3's ~0.39 s fixed
544-  cost. It is the trade decided above. A client that wants P18's rate for
545-  one long prompt can send it as interactive, which is not chunked.
546-- **A 262k-cell cache makes prefill attention twice as dear, at any
547-  depth.** A 2048-token pass at depth zero costs 366 ms of attention against
548-  178 ms in a 65k-cell cache (1926 against 1729 ms a pass). This morning's
549-  binary measures the same to 3 ms (1923 / 1728), so it predates C6, and
550-  every 262k configuration since P18 has paid it. P7 made *decode* cost the
551-  depth rather than the cache; some prefill kernel still costs the cache.
552-  That is the next prefill lever (below): agent prefill is 8.0 s at 262k
553-  cells against 7.3 at 65k.

559-  labels of `cmd/llm -graph -tokens 2048 -ctx 262144` against `-ctx 65536`
560-  will name it. It is ~10% of every prefill at the served context.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='CONCURRENCY.md'
s=open(p).read()
old_bullet=s[s.index('- **A 262k-cell cache makes prefill attention twice as dear, at any\n'):s.index('## Next')]
new_bullet='''- **A 262k-cell cache made prefill attention twice as dear, at any
  depth.** A 2048-token pass at depth zero cost 366 ms of attention against
  178 ms in a 65k-cell cache (1926 against 1729 ms a pass). It predated C6
  and every 262k configuration since P18 paid it. **Fixed the same day**
  (the next section): it was the indexer score's tail fill.

## The cache-size cost in prefill (done 2026-09-23)

**The indexer's score wrote one float a token for every pooled block the
cache holds, not the context.** Every block at or past `nBid` (the first
that is not whole) pools cell 0 and so shares one score, and P7 already
computed that score once. But `llm_attn_score_wmma.comp` then *filled* it
into all `nBlocks - nBid` entries of the row. That is 65 535 floats a token
at depth zero in a 262 144-cell cache, **512 MB a layer for a 2048-row
pass**, streamed out at ~24 GB/s. Nothing on the device reads those entries:
P14-1's block select stops at the last block a cell can reach, and the
expansion (the cell-select control arm) maps every tail cell to `deadBid`.
Only the host's `AttnGPU.Score()` readback, which the tests compare with the
reference's whole `indexer_score_tokens`, ever saw them.

So the kernel writes the one entry at `nBid`, and `Score()` fills the rest on
the host, so the tensor keeps the reference's shape. The scalar control
kernel (`LLM_ATTN_SCORE=scalar`) got the same change, so the two arms keep
one contract. `-attn -tokens 2048` found it in one run: `score` was 4.46 ms
a layer at 65k cells and 20.6 at 262k. After the fix it is **0.29 and 0.30**,
because the fill was most of the kernel at *any* cache size.

**It is bit-exact.** The selection reads the same scores. `TestGraphLogits`
reproduces its diagnostics to the digit through 48 layers (maxAbs 1.987e+00
at 19208, rms 3.314e-01, argmax 11751 against 561). `TestAttnGPUIndexer`
and `TestAttnGPUIndexer4k` compare the full tensor, tail included, against
the reference, and they pass because of the host fill. The attention, QSA
and graph gates pass (`-run 'TestAttn|TestQSA|TestGraphIsAChunkSplit|
TestGraphSlots|TestGraphDecodeRows'`, 49 s).

**At 48 layers**, shipped banks, `cmd/llm -graph -tokens 2048`, the old and new
binaries interleaved, two passes each (agreeing to 6 ms):

| cache | before | after | attention before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 262 144 cells | 1922 / 1916 ms (1067 tok/s) | **1696 / 1696 ms (1208 tok/s), +13%** | 365 → 149 ms |
| 65 536 cells | 1728 / 1723 ms (1187 tok/s) | **1688 / 1688 ms (1213 tok/s), +2.3%** | 178 → 143 ms |

The 262k cache now costs 8 ms more a pass than the 65k one, where it cost
194 ms.

**Against depth** at the served cache (`-depth -depths 0,64000,128000,192000
-pp 2048 -ctx 262144`, one sweep each). The fill was `nBlocks - nBid` a
token, so the gain shrinks as the context fills:

| depth | pp before | pp after | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1043.4 | **1170.2** | +12.2% |
| 64 000 | 984.4 | **1050.8** | +6.7% |
| 128 000 | 953.2 | **968.1** | +1.6% |
| 192 000 | 892.2 | **901.7** | +1.1% |

DECODE_PLACEHOLDER

**What still scales with the cache, and is left:** `idx` at `past == 0`
pools every block of the table (0.09 → 0.31 ms a layer, once a sequence),
because a later pass's dead block reads that fill. `select` is 0.21 →
0.38 ms a layer, probably the score rows' wider stride. Together they are
the 8 ms above.

'''
s=s.replace(old_bullet,new_bullet)
old_next='''- **The cache-size cost in prefill attention** (C6 above): find the kernel
  that still scales with `nKV` rather than the live cells at prefill. The
  labels of `cmd/llm -graph -tokens 2048 -ctx 262144` against `-ctx 65536`
  will name it. It is ~10% of every prefill at the served context.
'''
assert old_next in s
s=s.replace(old_next,'')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
sed -n '/^## Next/,$p' CONCURRENCY.md

content.text:
I've finished the next CONCURRENCY.md item: **the cache-size cost in prefill.** It was one kernel, the result is bit-exact, and prefill at the served 262k context is 13% faster at depth zero.

**The cause.** The indexer's score kernel wrote the same "dead" score into every pooled block the *cache* could hold, not just the ones the conversation had reached. At 262k cells that was 512 MB of writes a layer for each 2048-token chunk, or 16 ms of a 33 ms attention layer. Nothing on the GPU ever read those entries; only a readback that the tests use did.

**The fix.**
- `shaders/llm_attn_score_wmma.comp` and the scalar control kernel `llm_attn_score.comp` now write that score into one entry a token instead of up to 65k.
- `AttnGPU.Score()` (`llm/gpu_attn.go`) fills in the rest when it reads the tensor back, so the tests still compare the full reference shape.

**Checks.** All passed:
- **Whole model:** `TestGraphLogits` reproduces its diagnostics to the digit through all 48 layers (maxAbs 1.987e+00 at 19208, rms 3.314e-01).
- **Full score tensor:** `TestAttnGPUIndexer` and `TestAttnGPUIndexer4k` compare the whole tensor against the reference, including the part now filled on the host.
- **Other gates:** the attention, QSA and graph gates pass.

**Speed at 48 layers**, old and new binaries run alternately in the same hour:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| prefill pass, 262k cache | 1922 / 1916 ms | **1696 / 1696 ms (+13%)** |
| prefill pass, 65k cache | 1728 / 1723 ms | **1688 / 1688 ms (+2.3%)** |
| pp at 262k cache, depth 0 (3 runs each) | 1035-1039 tok/s | **1171-1175 tok/s** |
| pp at 262k cache, depth 64k (3 runs each) | 985-986 tok/s | **1046-1048 tok/s** |
| decode at depths 0 and 64k (3 runs each) | 34.08 / 32.71 tok/s | 34.16 / 32.76 tok/s (no change) |

- **Deeper contexts gain less:** the wasted writes shrank as the context filled, so the gain is +1.6% at 128k and +1.1% at 192k.
- **Long agent prompts:** I did not re-measure the 237k prompt through the server. My estimate is about +5% over a whole prefill of that length.
- **Cache size is now almost free:** a 262k cache costs 8 ms more a pass than a 65k one, down from 194 ms.

What remains of that 8 ms is two small kernels, written up in the new section. The one that runs on every pass costs ~2 ms of it and is probably not worth a stage.

CONCURRENCY.md has the new section, C6's note on this cost now points to it, the item is off **Next**, and there is a log line. I also updated the 262k memory note. The auto-committer will pick up the changes, so I haven't committed. `ai.service` was already stopped when I started, and I've left it stopped.

The next item in **Next** is what's left in a three-row batched decode pass: mostly the MoE, plus row-aware attention and DeltaNet kernels worth up to ~2 ms a row.
